title: Duchy of Livonia
capsule: The Duchy of Livonia was created by the Treaty of Vilnius of 28 November 1561 when the Livonian Order secularized itself and placed the Livonian Confederation under Polish-Lithuanian suzerainty, corresponding roughly to modern northern Latvia (Vidzeme and Latgale) and southern Estonia. Its successive grand dukes were the Jagiellonian and then Vasa kings of Poland-Lithuania; Jan Hieronimowicz Chodkiewicz served as its first resident governor from Sigulda Castle. Sweden progressively seized the duchy's territory during the Polish-Swedish War of 1621–1625, a conquest confirmed by the Truce of Altmark in 1629, after which the residual southeastern portion became the Inflanty Voivodeship before passing to Russia under Catherine the Great in 1772.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's territory is documented in the Treaty of Vilnius and subsequent Polish-Lithuanian administrative records; boundaries are well established, though the gradual Swedish conquest created zones of contested control between 1600 and 1629.
